metadata.title: The logo Skill
metadata.audience: Brutalist fellows already using Claude Code
metadata.note: Skill teardown of skills/make/logo/SKILL.md (SOURCE-SNAPSHOT SHA-256 badfb2bc…; supervisor's episode.source_sha256 213d82e1…). The `logo` skill appends one brand sting after a reel's last beat: one random-once pick of (animation technique × brand SVG × brand MP3) locked into the beat, aspect-aware, MP3-clocked with a padded tail so the jingle is never cut. Teaches: (1) the anatomy — SKILL.md doctrine, logo.py scaffolder, LogoOutro.tsx scene, logos/[brand]/ pool, runtime/remotion/public/logo-outro/ staging; (2) the six-step flow — resolve alias · pick or reuse · copy+pad mp3 · stage svg · append beat · render+recompile; (3) MP3 IS THE CLOCK — --tail pads silence, frame rounding/mux -shortest can only trim silence never sound; (4) RANDOM ONCE THEN LOCKED — pick recorded at shot.remotion.picked, rebuilds stable, --reroll re-randomizes; (5) POOL CURATION — draw is uniform over *.svg so the pool is the quality bar (medhavy: 42 drawable / 25 unique / 12 rejected); (6) drawOn IS EARNED — only eligible when the SVG is path-only (no text/image/gradient/mask); (7) FALSIFIABILITY: there is no logos/nik-bear-brown/ by design — @NikBearBrown uses ClaudeTitleOutro's slug-seeded pixel mascot instead per OUTRO-LOCK.md. This teardown IS a claude-liam reel, so the outro is ClaudeTitleOutro (hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK) — the folder chip on all inner composer beats is @HumanitariansAI per playlist. logo.py demoed live on a synthetic fixture reel in demo/ (three real runs captured in demo/logo-run.log: hai first pick, hai --reroll to fresh pick, hai locked reuse, medhavy fresh pick landing on drawOn). Portrait companion — native 9:16 layouts (SkillTeardown*916 wrappers, ClaudeComposerAsk916, BrutalistHesitantWriter916 with portrait-scale patch per feedback_hesitant_writer_portrait_scale, ClaudeVerdictArtifact916, ClaudeTitleOutro916). channel_title metadata deliberately omitted per feedback_channel_title_portrait_bleed.

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — hesitant writer corrects the fixed-per-brand read to the actual claim: one RANDOM pick per reel. Single-token trigger per BrutalistHesitantWriter contract.
beats.narration_text: The easy read — the one the word logo invites — is that every reel gets the same fixed brand sting. It does not. The logo skill spins a wheel across the brand's mark pool and jingle pool, one random pick per reel, then locks the pick into the beat so every rebuild is byte-for-byte identical. Random across reels, locked within one.

beats.role_note: Design decision 1 — THE MP3 IS THE CLOCK. --tail pads silence so frame rounding and mux -shortest can only trim silence, never sound.
beats.narration_text: First design decision, and it is the whole architecture. The MP3 is the clock. When logo dot py copies the jingle, it pads it with a trailing silence — one second by default — using ffmpeg apad. The padded length becomes the beat's durationS, and Remotion's calculateMetadata derives the frame count from it. The audible jingle therefore ends strictly inside the beat. Frame rounding, clip conform, and mux dash shortest can only ever trim silence. Never sound. Same law as the outro. Want a different length? Use a different mp3.

props.heading: The MP3 is the clock.
props.body: logo.py copies the jingle to mp3/beat-<BID>.mp3, pads it with a trailing silence (--tail, default 1.0s) via ffmpeg apad, and measures the padded file with ffprobe. That length becomes props.durationS; Remotion's calculateMetadata derives durationInFrames from it. The audible jingle ends STRICTLY inside the beat — frame rounding, clip conform, and mux -shortest can only trim silence.
props.quote: The MP3 is the clock — and the jingle is NEVER cut.

beats.role_note: Design decision 2 — RANDOM ONCE, THEN LOCKED. Pick recorded at shot.remotion.picked; rebuilds stable; --reroll re-randomizes.
beats.narration_text: Second decision, and it is the one that makes rebuilds honest. The pick is random exactly once. Animation, svg, mp3 — chosen by SystemRandom, then written into the beat itself at shot dot remotion dot picked. Every subsequent run finds that block and reuses it, so your review cut and your final master are byte-for-byte the same sting. Want a fresh spin? Dash dash reroll discards the lock, picks again, and force re-renders. That is the whole random-versus-deterministic contract in one field.

props.heading: Random once, then locked.
props.body: SystemRandom picks (animation × svg × mp3). The pick is written into the beat at shot.remotion.picked — so every re-run finds it and reuses it. Review cut = final master, byte for byte. --reroll discards the lock, picks fresh, and force re-renders. One reel = one lottery.
props.quote: Random once, then locked… re-runs reuse it, so rebuilds are stable.
props.sparkLine: Random across reels. Locked within one.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — There is no logos/nik-bear-brown/ pool by design. The Bear channel uses ClaudeTitleOutro's slug-seeded pixel mascot per OUTRO-LOCK.md — a different outro architecture that reads no files at all.
beats.narration_text: Falsifiability. Read the sources together and you find a deliberate hole. There is no logos slash nik-bear-brown pool. Not missing. Not a bug. By design. The at NikBearBrown channel uses ClaudeTitleOutro instead — a Remotion scene whose pixel mascot is drawn from tiny rects in code, seeded by the reel slug, and reads no files at all. That is the OUTRO-LOCK contract. Which is why this teardown's outro is ClaudeTitleOutro — the falsifiability beat's own evidence is that the logo skill is not universal. Every other channel gets the random sting. The Bear channel gets the deterministic mascot card.

props.sparkLine: One skill does not fit all channels.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — artifact card. Recapitulates the skill in six lines.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. The logo skill appends one brand sting per reel — random once, locked forever. The mp3 is the clock, padded with a silence tail so the jingle is never cut. The draw is uniform over the pool, so curating the pool is the actual quality work. drawOn is earned — it needs clean path data or it is dropped from the lottery. Aspect follows the reel — nine sixteen or sixteen nine, no re-code. And the at NikBearBrown channel deliberately opts out — that channel uses ClaudeTitleOutro's pixel mascot, not this skill.
